intro.role: You're a buyer at {{company.name}}, a sneaker chain in the UAE.
intro.setting: It's the first week of the new season. Six things need a decision from you, and none of them will wait.
intro.goal: Keep the shelves full without putting the company at risk.

playbook.title: {{company.name}} Buying Playbook
rules: If you can undo it within two weeks, decide it yourself.
Never commit the company beyond this season without the head of buying.
The head of buying's time is limited. Every call costs a day.

decisions.situation: 1,200 pairs of your best-selling runner have arrived, but the size split is off: too many small sizes, not enough large ones. The brand accepts returns within 14 days.

facilitator.note: Two-way door. Rule 1 — keep and rebalance.

options.label: Keep it and rebalance
options.immediate: The stores have stock by Wednesday.

deferred.headline: Runners back on {{company.name}} shelves within days.
deferred.standfirst: Small sizes moved to the right stores and large sizes were topped up.

grade.rationale: Undoable within two weeks — yours to decide.

options.label: Reject the delivery and wait for a corrected one
options.immediate: The brand promises a new shipment in three weeks.

deferred.headline: Empty shelves as {{company.name}} runner shortage drags on.
deferred.standfirst: Shoppers went to rivals while the corrected shipment was still weeks away.

grade.rationale: Waiting three weeks when you could rebalance now.

options.label: Call the head of buying
options.immediate: The head of buying calls back the next day: "Why are you asking me? Keep it."

deferred.headline: Runner restock slips a day.
deferred.standfirst: A call delayed a decision that was yours under the playbook.

grade.rationale: Middle — escalated a reversible call and lost a day.

decisions.situation: A brand rep offers 18% off next season's pre-order if you sign today for 4,000 pairs, double last season's order.

facilitator.note: One-way door. Needs head of buying — Rule 2.

options.label: Sign today
options.immediate: The rep is delighted and the order is confirmed.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} stuck with 1,800 unsold pairs after pre-order bet.
deferred.standfirst: Doubling last season's order without a check left excess stock.

grade.rationale: Committed beyond this season without approval.

options.label: Tell the rep you'll come back next week

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} pays full price for next season.
deferred.standfirst: Delaying without escalating meant the deal was gone.

grade.rationale: Middle — right to pause, wrong to wait without calling.

options.label: Call the head of buying
options.immediate: The head of buying joins the call and negotiates 12% off on 2,500 pairs.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} lands a smart pre-order deal.
deferred.standfirst: A smaller order with a real discount beat both extremes.

grade.rationale: Beyond this season — bring in the head of buying.

decisions.situation: A limited colourway sold 70% of its stock in four days. The brand has 60 pairs left in the region, and another retailer is asking for them.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} sells out limited drop in a week.
deferred.standfirst: Acting while stock was still available paid off.

grade.rationale: Reversible within two weeks — decide it yourself.

options.label: Wait until Friday to see if demand holds
options.immediate: By Friday, all 60 have gone to the other retailer.

deferred.headline: Limited colourway lands at rival store.

grade.rationale: Too slow on a call you could undo.

options.label: Call the head of buying
options.immediate: The head of buying says yes, but only 20 pairs are left by then.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} gets a third of the drop.
deferred.standfirst: Escalating a reversible reorder cost most of the allocation.

grade.rationale: Middle — right impulse, wrong to spend a day on it.

decisions.situation: A casual canvas line isn't selling: 400 pairs, with six weeks left in the season.

facilitator.note: Can you really undo a markdown?

options.label: Mark it down 40% across all stores

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} shoppers learn to wait for the sale.
deferred.standfirst: Full-price sales dip next season after a steep markdown.

grade.rationale: Clears stock, but trains shoppers to wait — light score.

options.label: Move it to the outlet and keep full price elsewhere
options.immediate: 250 pairs sell by the end of the season.

deferred.headline: Outlet quietly absorbs slow canvas line.
deferred.standfirst: Most stock cleared without training the whole chain to wait for sales.

grade.rationale: Best light option — clear stock without a chain-wide markdown.

options.label: Call the head of buying
options.immediate: A day later, the head of buying chooses the outlet with 20% off.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} clears canvas stock quietly.
deferred.standfirst: Similar outcome to the outlet move, a day later.

grade.rationale: Middle light — same idea, paid a day for the call.

decisions.situation: Sahm Athletics, an up-and-coming regional brand, offers you 12 months of exclusive UAE rights, with a 1,500-pair minimum and a dedicated wall in every store.

facilitator.note: Saying no can be a one-way door too.

options.label: Accept
options.immediate: The contract is signed and the walls go up.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}}'s exclusive brand stalls, 1,100 pairs unsold.
deferred.standfirst: A season-plus commitment without a check left dead stock on the walls.

grade.rationale: Beyond this season without the head of buying.

options.label: Decline politely
options.immediate: The brand thanks you for your time.

deferred.headline: Sahm Athletics launches at rival chain to queues.
deferred.standfirst: Saying no closed a door — costly but understandable.

grade.rationale: Middle softened — a one-way no without exploring a trial.

options.label: Call the head of buying
options.immediate: The head of buying negotiates a six-month trial in five stores, with 600 pairs.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} trial of regional brand pays off.
deferred.standfirst: A smaller, time-boxed exclusive beat both accept and hard decline.

decisions.situation: {{influencer.name}}, a local sneaker influencer with 1.2M followers, proposes a co-branded drop: 300 pairs, her name on the box, launching in three weeks.

facilitator.note: Can you turn a one-way door into a two-way one?

options.label: Agree. It's only 300 pairs.
options.immediate: Marketing is thrilled and the boxes go to print.

deferred.headline: {{influencer.name}} x {{company.name}} sells out, then the comments turn.
deferred.standfirst: Her controversy sticks to your brand after the drop.

grade.rationale: Light — small volume, but the brand risk was hard to undo.

options.label: Counter with a two-week trial promoting an existing shoe

deferred.headline: Influencer push lifts {{company.name}} runner sales.
deferred.standfirst: A trial on an existing shoe kept the upside without a co-branded box.

grade.rationale: Best light — turn a one-way into a two-way.

options.label: Call the head of buying
options.immediate: A day later, the head of buying suggests the same trial.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} tests the influencer waters.
deferred.standfirst: Same trial idea, a day later.

grade.rationale: Middle light — right outcome, paid a day.

chrome.managerHeading: Your decisions and your manager's review of them
chrome.managerSubhead: This is your manager's read, based on the company's buying playbook.
chrome.closing: When you are ready, return to the main workshop room ↗

tooSlow.name: Too slow
tooSlow.zero: Nothing waited that was yours to decide.
tooSlow.withBranches: Waited on decisions that were yours: {stops}.

tooFast.name: Too fast
tooFast.zero: Nothing went ahead that needed a check.

operator.name: The Buyer
operator.description: You moved fast on what you could undo, and slowed down on season-level bets.
operator.hover: Buyers move fast on reversible stock calls, and bring in the head of buying on season commitments.

escalator.name: The Checker
escalator.description: You kept things safe by calling up, even when the playbook said the call was yours.
escalator.hover: Checkers keep things safe by escalating, even when they could decide it themselves.
escalator.tip: If you can undo it within two weeks, decide it yourself.

cowboy.name: The Closer
cowboy.description: You kept deals moving, including commitments that weren't yours to make.
cowboy.hover: Closers keep deals moving, including season bets that needed the head of buying.
cowboy.tip: If you couldn't undo it this season, pause and call the head of buying.

bottleneck.name: The Hold-up
bottleneck.description: You held back on the reversible calls and rushed the season commitments.
bottleneck.hover: Hold-ups wait on easy stock moves and rush the big buying bets.
bottleneck.tip: Take the easy reversals on the spot. Slow down only when you couldn't undo it this season.

ui.weekBoth: You waited on decisions that were yours to make. But went ahead with some that needed a check.
ui.weekSlow: You waited on decisions that were yours to make.
ui.weekFast: You went ahead with some that needed a check.
ui.weekClear: Nothing waited that was yours to decide, and nothing went ahead that needed a check.
